data.name: Download_ProviderDescription
data.value:
Download audio or video from a source URL to a local file and optionally convert audio to the selected output format.
The selected provider determines supported sources and prerequisites.
Select or create a provider in **Provider** that supports your source URL. Open that provider's own **Quick Start** for its prerequisites, installation links and configuration. The available providers can be extended; their supported source types and prerequisites may differ.

data.name: Download_ToolsDescription
data.value:
Open the selected provider and follow its own setup guide.
If it uses external tools, create or link the corresponding tool objects there. Each tool's own **Quick Start** explains its installation and physical path. Reuse an existing tool configuration when several providers use the same installation.
The FlowBlock keeps the source URL, output directory and output format; provider and tool setup remains with those components.

data.name: Download_RunDescription
data.value:
Connect **Start → Media download**.
1. Enter a source URL or bind an input field. 2. Choose the output directory and format, e.g. MP3. 3. Optionally choose an audio bitrate and allow overwriting. 4. Run the flow and use **Success** and **File path** in subsequent blocks.
Progress is reported as throttled Info messages. Reopen these instructions using **Quick Start** in the FlowBlock's actions.

data.name: Tool_DownloadDescription
data.value:
Download the latest release essentials ZIP for Windows x64: [Download FFmpeg for Windows x64 (ZIP, latest release)]({0})
This Windows build is provided by Gyan, a distributor linked from the official FFmpeg page: [Official FFmpeg download page — other platforms and builds]({1})
Extract the ZIP. Keep **ffmpeg.exe** and **ffprobe.exe** together in its **bin** directory. The installation must be accessible on the machine executing the flow, including CLI/service runs.

data.name: Tool_PathDescription
data.value:
Set **Binary directory** to the folder containing the executables, e.g. **C:\Tools\ffmpeg\bin**. Select the directory, not the ffmpeg.exe file. An empty directory uses the executing process's PATH.
Link this **FFmpeg tools** object in each provider under **Shared FFmpeg tools**. You can reuse the same installation across several providers and FlowBlocks.

data.name: FFmpeg_WindowTitle
data.value: Set up direct media downloads with FFmpeg

data.name: FFmpeg_SourceHeadline
data.value: Use a direct media or manifest URL

data.name: FFmpeg_SourceDescription
data.value:
Link this provider to the **Media download** FlowBlock. Its URL must point directly to a media file or HLS/DASH manifest, e.g. **https://example.org/video.mp4** or **stream.m3u8**. A website page URL requires a site extractor such as yt-dlp.
**Video** copies streams into MKV; **Original audio** copies audio into MKA. **MP3**, **M4A** and **Opus** convert audio. Set the output folder and format on the FlowBlock.

data.name: FFmpeg_ToolsHeadline
data.value: Link FFmpeg tools and configure recording

data.name: FFmpeg_ToolsDescription
data.value:
Create or link **FFmpeg tools** under **Shared FFmpeg tools**. Its Quick Start explains the installation. No yt-dlp or Deno executable is needed for this provider.
For a live stream, set **Recording duration (seconds)** and a larger **Timeout** so recording can finish. For finite media, leave duration empty to read to the end. **Output name** is optional; empty generates a stable name from the URL. Use a distinct name for each source when specifying it yourself.
